mechanism_narrative: The four-week decline in WORKPLACES indicates more people are working away from fixed sites, which raises discretionary daytime shopping and dining visits. As the drop in WORKPLACES persists, RETAIL_REC should rise over the next four weeks relative to the prior four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES moved from -25.9 to -13.9 over the snapshot window
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES stabilizes or rises while RETAIL_REC still falls over the next 28 days, this trend-link hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated above baseline, more activity remains home-centered and short trips to retail and restaurants are delayed. If RESIDENTIAL remains above 8 points for the next week, RETAIL_REC should weaken over the following month.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL stays above 8 points for at least one full week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed positive at 10.6 in t-0w
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL remains above the threshold but RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days, the home-stay suppression mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals broader mobility recovery that expands access to retail districts. When both series move up together, RETAIL_REC should improve within two weeks and remain higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improved from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES continue rising together but RETAIL_REC does not improve within 2 weeks, the joint-access mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated PARKS usage reflects favorable outdoor conditions that spill into higher leisure shopping and restaurant traffic with a short lag. A sustained upswing in PARKS should push RETAIL_REC higher within one week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by 5 points or more week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS remained near -29 across the snapshot
failure_condition: If PARKS rises by at least 5 points week-on-week and RETAIL_REC does not rise in the following week, the outdoor-spillover hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If transit mobility is still deeply depressed, access to shopping corridors remains constrained and retail visits lag. When TRANSIT stays below -20, RETAIL_REC should continue to underperform over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT was -23.0 at t-0w and below -20 throughout the snapshot
failure_condition: If TRANSIT remains below -20 but RETAIL_REC rises above its prior four-week mean, the access-constraint hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Higher GROCERY_PHARM combined with higher RESIDENTIAL indicates substitution toward at-home provisioning, which reduces discretionary retail visits. When both series stay above baseline together, RETAIL_REC should fall over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed positive while RESIDENTIAL stayed positive
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM and RESIDENTIAL remain positive together but RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 28 days, the substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid recovery in WORKPLACES after a weak base usually precedes consumer out-of-home activity with a short lag. If WORKPLACES gains at least 3 points in a week, RETAIL_REC should move higher within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by 3 points or more week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved from -17.7 to -13.9 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES jumps by at least 3 points week-on-week but RETAIL_REC does not rise within 2 weeks, the workplace-to-retail transmission fails.

mechanism_narrative: In late-summer outdoor periods, PARKS and TRANSIT move together as mixed-purpose trips expand, and that shared mobility lift supports retail visits. This mechanism should operate only when PARKS is not collapsing and TRANSIT is improving at the same time, producing higher RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS and TRANSIT both remained substantially below baseline in the snapshot
failure_condition: If PARKS and TRANSIT improve together but RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines over the next 28 days, the seasonal co-mobility hypothesis is falsified.
